model: H618A (RGBIC Basic Wi-Fi + Bluetooth LED Strip Lights, 16.4 ft)
name: Govee RGBIC Basic LED Strip H618A (US)

radios.note: Govee's specs table gives 'Bluetooth+WiFi' as the control method; the Wi-Fi band isn't stated on the pages found.

matter.note: Govee's RGBIC strip specs table lists Matter as 'NO' for H618A.

apple_home.note: Not stated on the Govee pages found.

google_home.note: Govee's specs table has no Google column, and the Govee pages found don't state Google support for H618A.

alexa.note: Govee's RGBIC strip specs table lists Alexa as 'YES' for H618A, through Govee's own skill.

smartthings.note: Not stated on the Govee pages found.

home_assistant.note: H618A is on the supported list of Home Assistant's official Govee Light Local integration, which needs LAN control enabled on the strip.

hubRequired.note: Controlled from the Govee app over Wi-Fi or Bluetooth; no hub is mentioned.

localControl.note: Home Assistant's Govee Light Local integration talks to the strip over the LAN (local push); LAN control must be switched on in the Govee app.

lengthM.note: Govee lists one 5 m roll (16.4 ft). The specs table says it can't be cut.

multiZone.note: RGBIC means several colours at once along the strip.

power.note: Govee's specs table lists a power adapter at 24 V / 0.5 A.

summary: Govee H618A works with Alexa, and with Home Assistant over your local network through the official Govee Light Local integration. It's a 5 m (16.4 ft) RGBIC strip that connects by Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, no hub needed. Govee's specs table lists no Matter, and Apple Home, Google Home and SmartThings aren't confirmed.
caveats: Govee lists no Matter support for H618A.
Home Assistant's local control needs LAN control enabled in the Govee app.
Google Home and Apple Home are not confirmed by the Govee pages found.
Govee's specs table says the strip can't be cut.
